featured_reviews.review_text: I would like to give them ZERO STARS FOR EVERYTHING. THE WORST RESTAURANT I HAVE EVER BEEN IN MY LIFE. THE OWNER IS ARROGANT,RUDE,ABUSIVE. He caused mental harassment and torture to us as customers. He said even the @commissionerofmumbaipolice can't do anything to me. He said I don't care about the @bmc. His license should be cancelled for such behaviour. I would request to avoid using this place to save your own self respect. Over charged food items, poor quality, stale food. featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Dear Nikita,

Thank you for your dramatic review.

It is quite remarkable that a disagreement over a chargeable portion of Szechuan sauce has somehow transformed into allegations involving harassment, torture, police authorities, licensing authorities, food quality, pricing, and practically everything else under the sun.

For the benefit of readers, the facts are simple. You demanded a complimentary item that was clearly mentioned as chargeable on the menu. When your demand was politely declined, you chose to express your disappointment through a review filled with exaggerated accusations rather than facts.

It is also interesting that despite claiming the food was stale, overpriced, of poor quality, and that the restaurant is the "worst" you have ever visited, the central issue during your visit was obtaining free sauce rather than any concern about the food itself.

Our restaurant has served thousands of customers over the years and continues to do so successfully. We are happy to provide excellent food and service, but unfortunately we are unable to provide unlimited complimentary items simply because someone demands them.

We respect genuine feedback. What we do not take seriously are fictional stories written in anger because a clearly chargeable item was not given free of cost.

We wish you all the best in finding a restaurant that includes complimentary extras with every order. As for us, we will continue serving our customers with transparency, consistency, and the same menu policies that apply equally to everyone.

featured_reviews.name: Subodh Mishra
featured_reviews.review_text:
While Juhu is famous for its beach snacks and high-end cafes, the real magic happens in the kitchens that treat seafood with the respect it deserves. This isn't just a meal; it’s a deep dive into the culinary traditions of the Konkan coast.
The Ambiance
Don't expect minimalist chic. The vibe here is "busy Sunday lunch." It’s loud, efficient, and smells heavenly. The decor is usually simple because the owners know you aren't there to look at the walls—you’re there for the crab.
The Standout Dishes
Bombil Fry (Bombay Duck): A local must-have. It’s light, crisp on the outside, and melts like butter the moment it hits your tongue. If it doesn't crunch, it's not authentic.
Butter Garlic Pepper Crab: This is the messiest, most rewarding dish on the menu. The meat is succulent, and the sauce is so rich you’ll want to mop it up with a Neer Dosa.
Surmai (Kingfish) Thali: For the solo diner or the traditionalist. A thick, spicy masala fry served alongside a bowl of soul-warming Sol Kadhi (a pink, tangy coconut milk appetizer).
The Verdict
The service is brisk—they expect you to eat, enjoy, and make room for the next hungry patron. It’s a bit pricey compared to street food, but for the freshness of the catch, it’s worth every rupee.
Pro Tip: Always ask for the "Catch of the Day" before looking at the menu. If the Pomfret is fresh, don't overthink it—just order it.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Hi Subodh, 
Experiencing the flavors of the Konkan coast is truly what dining is all about, and it’s wonderful to hear that our seafood dishes resonated with you. The Bombil Fry and Butter Garlic Pepper Crab are favorites for a reason, and it’s delightful to know they stood out during your visit. Your pro tip about the "Catch of the Day" is sure to help other guests maximize their experience!
Regards, 
Mahesh Lunch Home

featured_reviews.name: Chand De Silva
featured_reviews.review_text:
We were looking for a good thali set near our hotel and found Curry Leaf through a Google search. To our surprise, it was within easy walking distance!
​They offer both veg and non-veg options. We tried the Prawns Thali and the Chicken Thali, both were delicious and very reasonably priced. The service was impressively fast, and the manager was particularly helpful, making sure we had a great experience.
​When we visited during lunch, the place was filled with working professionals, which is always a good sign of consistent quality. Definitely a great spot for an authentic, quick, and affordable meal!

featured_reviews.name: Sarita Sahu
featured_reviews.review_text: I recently visited your restaurant and was disappointed with the overall experience. There were bees and mosquitoes flying around the dining area, which made it uncomfortable to enjoy the meal. Additionally, the service was not attentive, and the food served was not what I had ordered. Receiving the wrong dish added to the inconvenience. I hope you take this feedback seriously and work on improving hygiene, order accuracy, and service quality.

featured_reviews.name: Rutwiz Chipkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
We were a group of 15 people who visited this place for seafood and chicken thalis after seeing the 4.5 rating. Honestly, the reviews don’t match the actual experience at all.

Let me highlight the issues:

1. We requested regular drinking water, but it was served in flimsy paper glasses. When we asked for proper glasses, we were told only 6 were available—which is unacceptable for a place handling large groups.

2. The dining area had a serious mosquito problem. We had to repeatedly ask for some solution. Initially, the staff denied having anything, but only after most of us complained did they bring something to address it.

3. We ordered 7 Surmai thalis. While the fish was fresh, the portion size was disappointing and far below what is typically expected in a thali.

4. The solkadi was extremely diluted, lacking flavor, and the dry fish chutney portion was negligible—almost like a pinch.

Overall, this was a very underwhelming experience, especially considering the rating and expectations. Definitely not worth the hype.

featured_reviews.name: Aaren Martis
featured_reviews.review_text: Really disappointed, came here after the reviews but there is so much of colour added in the food, that my lips and fingers are still orange from afternoons thalis. Taste wise the food wasn't bad but adding so much of colour is really unacceptable. Also, adding an extra fee for gas should be informed to customers before they have lunch so they can be aware about it, rather than adding it and we need to figure out why 10% of the bill amount is added extra. I understand prices have increased but please cut down cost as everyone's is affected by the global crisis.

featured_reviews.name: Eshaan Shetty
featured_reviews.review_text: Had a really good experience at Curry Leaf Kalina. The Bombil Thali was fresh and flavourful, and we also loved the Chicken Fried Rice, Kalimiri Kebab, and Ghee Roast – all well cooked and tasty. Nice family vibe, quick service, and good value for money. Will surely visit again!

featured_reviews.name: Kajal Grover
featured_reviews.review_text: Curry Leaf Kalina serves delicious food with generous portions at extremely reasonable prices. With space for around 100 guests, it’s perfect for birthdays, parties, and bulk orders. On busy days, service can be slightly slow, but the overall experience is still excellent.

featured_reviews.name: Aakanksha
featured_reviews.review_text: The vibe here is warm and welcoming, with the staff being extremely polite and attentive. What’s also nice to see is that the place attracts a mix of families and a lot of corporate crowd as well, which shows how popular it is in Kalina. At times it does get quite busy, but that only adds to the lively atmosphere and charm of the restaurant.

All the staff is very friendly and food quality is also awesome!!!
Must try -- Veg anchow rice.

featured_reviews.review_text:

featured_reviews.name: Veikho Asanii
featured_reviews.review_text:
One of the pioneer North East restaurants in Mumbai.
Thotrin Cafe, located in the heart of Kalina, serves authentic Northeast dishes. The restaurant has two floors of seating and offers a wide variety of food. I’ve tried almost their entire menu — from Kangshoi to noodles, Thotrin Special to pot rice — and everything has been excellent.

It’s also a great place and only NE outlet for bulk orders. Special thanks to Amei Yaomi for his kind-hearted service towards customers. Highly recommended — you will never regret it. They truly feed you well!

featured_reviews.name: Yoh
featured_reviews.review_text:
This Manipuri restaurant has been around for a while now and is serving some delicious soul food. I have been to restaurant and also ordered from there a few times.

Started off with the Seisa salad which is crunchy and pungent; not for the faint hearted. The Smoked Hoksa with Aloo and Bamboo shoot is my favourite currently, paired with their Thotrin rice. The innards masala curry was also delicious. I ask for the Ngari (fermented dry fish with King chilli) which is a flavour bomb. I tried the chicken salad which was not as impressive.

I’m looking forward to trying more of their meals and I’m sure each one will be authentic and its own way.

featured_reviews.name: Beni Ngullie
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Famous North East restaurant in Mumbai, which serves homely made food !!
Loved it.. i think this is the fourth or fifth time i have been there and i am still amazed on how they win me over everytime!!!

Go for it !! The price and the food !! Just so good !!

Please do try the fermented banana wine !!

You will love every bit of it!!

featured_reviews.name: geethu k gopi
featured_reviews.review_text: I would love to give them 5 star but honestly, the atmosphere was very uncomfortable. The food was great.. the space is small was also okay, but the smell from the meat shop near it was so uncomfortable and so strong of dead chickens that It made me nauseous..i couldn’t enjoy eating momos for it packed and ate it at home. The staff is so sweet and nice…a small suggestion for the owners..your food is great. May be you should move to another space and let everyone enjoy the food breathing good air..

featured_reviews.name: Sam Jerry
featured_reviews.review_text: The food was excellent. We ordered thukpa soup and crispy chicken rice it was so delicious tangy flavour. The soup was tempting. The staff lady was also very sweet and dedicated. The place was cozy

featured_reviews.name: Apollo Eliazer
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you want to eat NAGA Cuisine, Tangkhul Cuisine this is the perfect spot to eat.
Ask the staff about the food to understand what's the content of each dish, also for recommendations.
Ask for the level of spice before ordering if you're having low spice tolerance.

Over-all it is an experience. If you don't have northeastern friends to cook for you or have never visited the northeast - this is definitely going to be a great experience and a good investment.

Come here only focusing on food, if you care too much about ambience, don't come here. Cleanliness is maintained and there is a clean washroom too.

The staff were friendly and helpful, and the overall atmosphere was relaxed and comfortable. You can really tell that this restaurant focuses on quality seafood and good taste.

featured_reviews.name: Taara Todkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had a great experience at this restaurant today with Kielash. We ordered an array of seafood and other foods - sukkah crab, tandoori chicken, bombil, bangda fry (mackerel) and seafood biryani.

The crab and bombil were amazing both flavourful and rich - would highly recommend! The seafood biryani was good and the tandoori chicken was moist and delicious. Our only issue with the food today was the mackerel as although the masala was nice the fish itself did not taste as fresh.

Service was amazing as the employees were very helpful.

featured_reviews.name: Dr. CHAITANYA JASTI
featured_reviews.review_text: As the street amazes you with some great eateries, Ferry Wharf satisfies you with some good dishes to offer. Seafood here is specail and the coconur base Prawn gravy is a must try with appam (Tiffin Box).  The bamboo biriyani seems to be popular here, but for someone who is well versed with the authentic bamboo biriyani from eastern ghats, doesn't find this satisfying, though a decent attempt.

featured_reviews.review_text: Nice sea food. Quite delicious. Their solkadhi had garlic ! Which I found little strange. Traditional solkadhi do not have garlic. They might have experimentes not sure

Being a vegetarian, I ordered Cream Brocolli, Cheese Stuffed Potatoes as starters and dal and rice for mains. I would like to recommend the Brocolli starter and the cheese naan is to die for!

My non-vegetarian company tried prawns fish thali, rava fish fry and chicken kebabs along with some other dishes. But everything in non-veg section was amazing. The staff also let us pick up a crab for pictures.

The staff paid attention to our needs and were very good hosts! Loved my experience. Won't mind visiting again!

Great food, great flavours! We went here for lunch on a Friday afternoon  - it was quite packed - recommend reservation.

We ordered: Bombil fry and Surmai for starters. Followed by Prawns Gassi, Rawas Pulimunchi with Neer dosa and Malabar paratha. I personally liked the curries with the neer dosa better. We finished off with kulfi and caramel custard for dessert.

The food and flavours were exceptional. The best part was the curry tasting experience which helped immensely in the ordering process. One of their staff came with a big plate of their different curries - gassi, Malvani, pulimunchi, Goan, etc. He let us taste all of those and explained the flavour profile of each. This was such a huge help because just reading off of a menu card can only do so much.

Felt it was a bit pricey but overall enjoyed the meal a lot. As a quick feedback, I’d urge them to move away from blue lighting and install more yellow lights. :)

Dishes are little bit pricey but taste is awesome.

featured_reviews.name: Roosa and Gigi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mahesh is one place that never really disappoints. The seafood is always fresh and delicious, which is what keeps me coming back. Every dish I’ve tried so far tastes well-prepared and satisfying, especially if you’re craving something simple but flavorful.
What I like even more about this branch compared to others is how spacious it is. It feels more comfortable to dine in, with enough room that you don’t feel too cramped or rushed, even when there are a lot of customers.
It’s a reliable spot for good seafood. Fresh food, decent prices, and a more relaxed dining space make it a better experience for me personally.

featured_reviews.name: Himanshu Desai
featured_reviews.review_text:
The same great taste since decades. Had a big tandoori pomfret, mutton ghee roast, chukka mutton, fried surmai and prawn gassi. All this with neer dosai and brown rice.

The four ladies with us found excellent vegetarian choices and were very happy.

The drinks as usual were great.

featured_reviews.name: Sankar Parida
featured_reviews.review_text: It is one of the best restaurant for sea foods. We had tasted here squid, lobster, crab soup, surma, pomphret, Bombay duck. All items are tasty, service also very fast. One may select the fish prior to cooking also.

featured_reviews.name: VIBHUTI SIRSAT
featured_reviews.review_text:
Jugnu is a must-visit!
The food, service, and ambiance are all incredible. We had a perfect time—the dishes were delicious and the atmosphere is stunning and perfect for groups. Seriously, every corner is Insta worthy! Highly recommend for a fun night out with friends.

featured_reviews.name: SHIRLEY GAIKWAD
featured_reviews.review_text:
I wouldn’t recommend this place.
I visited after a long break, hoping for the same experience Mahesh was once known for, but it was extremely disappointing. The ghee roast tasted odd, and the masalas were clearly undercooked. I felt nauseous after eating it. The soups were bad too, they tasted burnt, and even after asking for a remake there was barely any improvement.
The restaurant is expensive, which wouldn’t be an issue if the food justified the price, but this was absolutely ridiculous.
The neer dosa was raw and felt like one dosa had been cut in half and served as two. The squid was just about bearable, but by then the overall experience had already ruined the meal.
We left feeling completely disappointed. What made it worse was that even after complaining to the manager, nothing was done to address our concerns.
Mahesh used to be much better. Sadly, that quality is gone now.
Please save your money and skip this place.

featured_reviews.name: Hitesh Harisinghani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Tucked away in a tiny lane in Vakola, this cozy restaurant has barely 6–7 tables, giving it an intimate, no-frills charm. What truly stands out is the hospitality — the staff makes you feel like you're being fed at someone’s home, and that love reflects in the food.

Their traditional meal/thali is served on a banana leaf and is pure comfort. It includes 4 vegetables, 4 varieties of curries, pickle, chutney, and unlimited rice — wholesome, hearty, and incredibly satisfying.

Also, tried -

Surmai Pollichatu – Absolutely the BEST! Perfectly cooked, bursting with flavor, and paired beautifully with soft appams. A must-order.

Buff Fry – Delicious, flavorful, and a perfect companion to parottas.

Prawns Fry – Took a bit long to arrive and was just okay compared to the other standout dishes.

The best part? Four of us ate to our heart’s content for just ₹830! They even served papad and a small cup of payasam on the house. Incredible value for money.

Great food, warm service, generous portions, and prices that make you want to come back again — honestly, what more could you for..

featured_reviews.name: Bhavya Bhat
featured_reviews.review_text: Visited Kalavara Kitchen on a Sunday thinking it would be packed, but luckily got a table right away. It’s a small, quaint place with a warm vibe, and the staff were super friendly and welcoming. We tried the Kerala Meal (3.5/5),Chicken Kizhi Biryani (3.5/5), and Payasam (5/5) Portions were decent for the price. Overall, a cozy spot worth visiting once in a while!

featured_reviews.name: Vidya Bhat
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had ordered their Potichor, which is like a wholesome Kerala-style meal packed in a banana leaf.

I had ordered three types — veg, chicken, and egg.

The quantity is really generous for the price, one Potichor is easily enough for two people, especially if you’re someone who doesn’t eat too much rice. A small suggestion to make the experience would be to give some more Sambhar as the rice gets a bit dry. Also, adding a pappadam on the side would make the meal absolutely perfect!

Overall a good dish to explore Kerala style meal 👍🏻

PS. The content of Potichor is Rice, Beans Sabji, Raw Banana Chana Sabji, Pickle, Coconut Based Chutney, Protein of your choice(Omelette or Chicken Fry pieces), Sambhar, Aviyal and curd based curry.

featured_reviews.name: REENA SAM
featured_reviews.review_text: If you’re craving authentic Kerala food in Mumbai, this place is a real lifesaver! The meals taste homely with the right Kerala flavors-spice done perfectly. featured_reviews.name: K. “ContentName” F.
featured_reviews.review_text:

The staff were friendly. However, not all seemed well-informed about the menu items, which could be a bit of a drawback if you're looking for recommendations or ingredient details.

I ordered Rajavinte Chattichoru and Malabar Chicken Korma , both of which had strong, authentic Kerala flavors. That said, I found both dishes a bit too spicy for my personal taste.

A concern I had was related to how the cleaning mop was stored alongside banana leaves. Something they need to change.

Overall, this place is great for solo meals or hanging out with friends. I wouldn’t recommend it for a date. I will certainly visit again to try the other dishes. Yet to find my favorite.

Rajavinte Chattichoru - 3/5 (Multiple dishes in a bowl instead of a bannana leaf. Quantity sufficient for 3 people. The taste of tamrind was too strong)

featured_reviews.name: Siddhesh Kotian
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Theeram recently with a friend, and it turned out to be a hidden gem for Kerala cuisine lovers—especially non-veg enthusiasts. However, there are a few things you should know before planning your visit.

The restaurant is located in a narrow lane of Kalina, Santacruz East, and does not have any dedicated parking, so you’ll need to manage that on your own. It’s a small, cozy place with limited seating—around four tables for four and two tables for two, so it’s not ideal for large groups. Ambience is simple, nothing fancy, but the focus here is clearly on food.

The menu is purely Kerala-style and is a treat for those who enjoy authentic regional flavors. However, it’s written in a local Kerala dialect/accent, which can be a bit tricky to understand. I recommend asking the staff to explain the dishes before you order.

We tried:
•	Seafood Soup – Flavorful, slightly spicy, and full of rich coastal taste. Highly recommend.
•	Tawa Prawns – Slightly undercooked/raw in texture, which I personally didn’t mind, but others may want to be cautious, especially those prone to allergies.
•	Fried Chicken – Crispy, but overly salty and quite oily. Not my favorite.
•	Egg Parotta – Soft, flaky, and tasty—this was a hit!
•	Shevaya Payasam – A perfect ending to the meal. Mild, sweet, and authentic.

The service was on the slower side, and a few items we wanted were unavailable, so we had to adjust our order based on what was available. That was a bit disappointing, but the flavors made up for it.
If you’re a non-veg lover or someone from Kerala missing homestyle food, this place is definitely worth a visit. Don’t expect a lavish setup—come for the food.

featured_reviews.name: Nikhil
featured_reviews.review_text:
Absolute Horrifying Experience.

Request all people to read through before visiting/ordering.

AFTER SEEING OTHER REVIEWS, I FIND OUT THAT THIS IS A VERY COMMON COMPLAINT SINCE YEARS AND THERE SEEMS TO BE NO CHANGE.

I had prebooked 3 Onam Sadhya for lunch. I was told to visit the place and pick it up at 12:30pm. (Was prebooked the previous day)

As per normal practice, pre-booked orders must me kept ready to collect at the time the customer has been called to collect.

I travelled 14kms to reach the restaurant at the appointed time to collect my order. On arrival, firstly we are made to wait outside in the rain on the street. After waiting for more than 1 hour, these guys still didn't give me my order and in front of me 8-10 Zomato/Swiggy guys came and collected their orders and left.

The guys at the restaurant, a young woman at the reception and a malayali guy were not at all interested in serving and cluless. Speaking rudely, and absolutely shamelessly despite waiting for an hour asking me to wait for some more time.

Firstly, atleast in Mumbai, the restaurant shouldn't have people who don't speak Hindi to adress customers.

Frustrated, I left from the venue as it was already late for lunch. Kept calling the contact number provided online atleast 50 times only to be picked up and hung up by them while we are speaking. After trying more than 50 times, somehow got in touch with them, and at 2:30 pm I was told that they will deliver the order to my residence.

After all the hassle, at 4:36pm I was told by the restaurant that my order will arrive in 10 mins. The order actually arrived at 5:38pm.

After receiving the order, I find out they have sent me only 2 Meals while I ordered for 3. On calling the person coordinating, he firstly denied saying they sent the correct order and were blaming it on the delivery guy. This person, Name: Shahid Kappur, started speaking rudely and was shouting at me and was asking me to return the order that I had received.

After calling the restaurant multiple times, they finally accepted their mistake and agreed to send me another sadhya box. This box reached my at 7:30pm.

All this was ordered for Lunch and was supposed to be picked up at 12:30pm.

To top all of this, after opening the food, I find out that banana leaves were not provided in two Sadyas, sambar was not provided in one sadya. The papad was soggy and the payadan too doggy. Food was not packed properly (check the pictures).

I've been ordering Onam Sadya from Theeram since the last 3-4 years. I was a big fan of their food but this time it was a horrific experience and surely this restaurant has lost a customer.

For people considering Onam Sadya, please consider the following restuarants and you will surely have a better experience:
1. Santosham (Multiple Outlets)
2. Coconut Kitchen (Chembur)
3. Taste of Kerala (Fort)
And many more Kerala restaurants serve onam sadhya.

This restaurant has a very small seating capacity, the food is stored/prepared in a store/room across the road and the servers are walking on the street in the rain with containers containing the food open for contamination.

Absolutely horrific and unacceptable.

featured_reviews.name: Badri Nathan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Theeram yesterday for lunch. Very disappointed with the quality of food. I decided to taste Kerala Paratha & the Appam   with the vegetable Korma. Malabar Paratha+Korma is the famous combination in South India and particularly in Kerala. Unfortunately this Kerala specialty Restaurant messed it up.

The order was for one Paratha and one Appam. But they served 2 Parathas and the Appam never came nor the waiter bothered to ask.

The place is a shanty converted into a small restaurant type. On enquiry, I found out that a Kerala cook prepare few items in the morning and goes away. Rest is managed by some UP cook. The eating area was not lit up properly and I felt like sitting in an illegal Country Liquor joint. At the end, I asked if they have Jaggery based rice Payasam. They said yes and served the sugar payasam. Again I asked for Jaggery based Payasam, which was more liquid and extremely sweet.

Overall experience was not good. I will not recommend this place if you are looking for authentic Kerala Veg Food.

featured_reviews.name: Vipul G
featured_reviews.review_text:
Wok express is spreading its wings slowly but firmly across the city.. Most of them are like takeaway joints .. I happened to visit their bkc outlet on Sunday eve, my first experience at wok express, n it was good.. Wok express do serve oriental food at very reasonable rates.. The bkc outlet has 3 tables n few chairs to sit.. It's a very clean hygienic place.. I started here with zesty lemon n coriander soup.. This healthy n delicious soup had refreshing combination of lemon, coriander n veggies in it with a thick consistency .. We tried crispy tempura roll sushi n they were scrumptious.. Carrot, Onion, Tempura flour and Sesame oil rolled in sweet and sour rice are served along with soya sauce.. It was too good n one of the best sushi I have ever had.. Had kung pao potatoes n it was also very good .. Baby potatoes, cooked in Chinese sauce, are served along with roasted peanuts on it.. It was delectable n quite filling one.. We also tried chilli Paneer bao n I found it ok.. Chopped pieces of succulent Paneer are marinated well in spicy chilli basil sauce n are served in super soft fluffy bao.. I found it too much saucy to my liking.. Wok express is known for its wok n they here do serve some really amazing wok our here.. One can directly order for chef recommended wok box which I guess will be great to do.. One can also customise n choose between rice n noodles, sauces, veggies n condiments n prepare wok according to their liking if you are particular about what u eat.. Also there are sizes to choose from n along with combo deals with drinks it's very reasonable.. I had Bangkok ramen noodles n it was too good.. This wok box had ramen noodles along with veggies n sauce were topped with burnt garlic.. It was hot, tasty n treat to my taste buds.. Food overall was good here n let me warn u if u don't like medium spicy or spicy food this place is not for you.. We also tried popcorn n peach iced bubble tea n I found both to be good in flavour but frankly Tapioca pearls in it were not that great n i will recommend to try bubble tea without tapioca pearls in it.. Will like the management to work on tapioca pearls n improve on it.. Service was good n staff were very helpful with their recommendations.. As food is prepared fresh expect 10/15 mins wait for ur order.. Overall it was decent experience out here n I'm surely trying their other woks served out here in future

My recommendations - Zesty lemon n coriander soup, crispy tempura roll sushi, kung pao potatoes, Bangkok ramen noodles

Visited this place with my ex-colleagues, and to be honest, The vibe of the place is great for spending time with family.

We ordered quite a few dishes including prawns masala fry, bombil masala, bombil rawa fry, grilled pomfret, crab lollipop, chicken, and finally prawns biryani.

Talking about the food, the crab lollipop was interesting. It obviously felt like frozen food, but the taste was still good. However, most of the seafood dishes were a little disappointing for us. The fish dishes were not spicy enough and lacked that strong flavor we were expecting. The stuffed pomfret was just okay-okay and felt more like boiled fish rather than properly fried.

We also ordered a chicken dish and specifically requested it to be spicy, but unfortunately, it turned out a bit sweet, and none of us really liked it.

But the highlight of the meal was definitely the prawns biryani. It was really, really good and honestly the best dish we had there.

If there are two dishes I would recommend to anyone visiting, it has to be the Bombil Fry and Peri Peri Bombil. They are easily my brother’s and my absolute favourites perfectly crispy, full of flavour, and something we end up ordering almost every single time.

And no meal here feels complete without the Kokum Sarbat or Kokum Soda. That refreshing, tangy punch of flavour just balances the seafood so well and makes the whole experience even better.

Good food, great flavours, and the comfort of family dinners this place truly feels special to us. Easily one of the best seafood restaurants and definitely a spot we’ll keep coming back to.

featured_reviews.review_text:
This was the final restaurant I attended on my trip and a great place to end on.

Unfortunately at the time of our attendance the A/C was not in working order which the manager/owner advised on prior to entering, however we still went in as they had fans going on.

Didn't plan to eat a lot but to take in the delights on offer as again this was a place recommended.

We were given good information by the manager on some of the dishes and on ordering the food arrived after a short time. temperatures were on point and flavours were amazing. The prawn starters were so good, especially the Prawns Garlic Butter, so much so we ordered another tray. I also order the Mutton Chops Ghee Roast and as it sat in front of me my mouth was watering. Spice level on this was perfect, had a nice little kick but was really enjoyable and not in a overpowering way. I found that the chop may have been slightly overdone to my liking, however this didn't take the enjoyment away from it.

The meals ordered were enjoyed by everyone in the party which also included children (they really enjoyed the Prawns Garlic Butter). Pricing of the meals and overall was very reasonable and this place is worth a visit if you have never been. I will look to return here again if I visit Mumbai again.

I recently visited Golden Wave Restaurant in Santacruz, Mumbai, for dinner with family and friends. The restaurant has a pleasant ambience with comfortable seating and a relaxed atmosphere, making it a good place for an evening meal.

We started our dinner with the Chicken Tandoori, which was well-marinated, nicely cooked, and packed with authentic smoky flavors. The chicken was tender and served fresh, making it the highlight of our meal. For the main course, we ordered the Mutton Dum Biryani. The biryani had aromatic rice and flavorful spices, while the mutton was cooked well and complemented the dish nicely.

However, the overall dining experience was affected by a couple of drawbacks. The service was noticeably slow, and we had to wait longer than expected for our food to arrive. While the quality and taste of the dishes were satisfactory, the portion sizes felt quite small considering the prices charged. This made the meal seem less value-for-money than we had anticipated.

That said, the restaurant's ambience and the taste of the food were enjoyable enough to make the visit worthwhile. If the management improves the speed of service and offers more generous portions, the overall experience would be significantly better.

Overall, Golden Wave Restaurant offers decent food in a pleasant setting, but there is room for improvement in service efficiency and portion sizes. I would rate my experience 3 out of 5 stars.

Dynasty: The Indo-Chinese Restaurant That Doesn’t Need Buzz
Five stars aren’t enough, but they’ll have to do.
Dynasty operates in that rare territory where quality speaks louder than Instagram followers. This unpretentious neighborhood spot has mastered the art of authentic Indo-Chinese cooking — the kind that requires skill, not shortcuts.
Order the Chicken Lollipop and you’ll understand immediately. Each piece is a study in balance: crisp exterior, succulent interior, perfectly seasoned. The Manchow Soup arrives with the kind of umami depth that makes you wonder why other restaurants even bother. The Crispy Spinach Chicken demands respect, while the Crispy Thread Chicken delivers texture with purpose. These aren’t interpretations — they’re the genuine article.
But the real revelation lies in the Sour Chili and Sichuan dips. Layered, bold, and unapologetically complex, they’re the kind of accompaniments that transform a meal into an experience. The lemon iced tea cuts through it all with perfect timing.
What distinguishes Dynasty, though, is the service. The team moves with purpose, never intrusive, always present. It’s a family restaurant in the truest sense — one that makes you feel like you belong.
In a city saturated with forgettable Indo-Chinese, Dynasty reminds you why authenticity never goes out of style.

Dynasty Restaurant, Khar West: A Chinese Culinary Journey

Dynasty Restaurant in Khar West, Mumbai, is a haven for Chinese food enthusiasts. This popular eatery has been delighting taste buds with its authentic and flavorful dishes for years. Whether you're craving spicy, tangy, or sweet, Dynasty has something to offer.

One of the must-try dishes at Dynasty is their Crispy Spinach Paneer. This vegetarian delight features tender cubes of paneer coated in a crispy batter and tossed with fresh spinach. The combination of textures and flavors is simply irresistible. For a refreshing drink to complement your meal, try their Ice Lemon Tea. The tartness of the lemon combined with the sweetness of the tea makes it a perfect thirst quencher.

If you're looking for something spicy, the Paneer Chilli is a great option. Tender pieces of paneer are stir-fried with a spicy chili sauce, making it a fiery dish that will leave your taste buds tingling. For a unique twist on Chinese cuisine, try the Schezwan Crispy Veg. This dish features mixed vegetables coated in a crispy batter and tossed in a spicy Schezwan sauce.

For a satisfying main course, consider the Veg Burnt Garlic Rice or the Veg Malaysian Noodles. Both dishes are packed with flavor and are sure to leave you feeling full and satisfied. Dynasty also offers a variety of Indian Chinese dishes, combining traditional Indian flavors with Chinese cooking techniques.

To start your meal, the Manchow Soup is a classic choice. This flavorful soup is packed with vegetables and a hint of spice. For a refreshing and tangy drink, try the Sweet and Salty Lime Soda. The combination of sweet and salty flavors is a unique and refreshing treat.

Whether you're a seasoned Chinese food lover or new to the cuisine, Dynasty Restaurant in Khar West is a must-visit. With its delicious food, friendly service, and inviting atmosphere, it's no wonder why this restaurant is so popular among locals and tourists alike.
